_what: Repository names that are DEAD — deleted or renamed away on GitHub — together with the date each died and where its contents went. Read by tooling/ci/assert-no-dead-repo-names.mjs, which refuses any LIVE surface that still names one.
_whyThisFileExists: On 2026-09-06 the Renovate workflow was still listing globalonlinedeveloper/Nikatru_Extensions_Public in RENOVATE_REPOSITORIES, twelve hours after that repository was deleted, and every scheduled run had been failing since. Nothing could have caught it: no guard knew the name was dead. A dead name is not a spelling mistake, it is a fact with a date, so it is declared here as data and enforced by one guard rather than re-derived by each reader.
_theRule: A name goes in this list the day the repository stops answering. It is NEVER removed — a name that is revived is a new fact and gets its own `revived` field, because deleting the row would silently re-license every stale reference the guard has been holding back.
_scope: LIVE surfaces only: workflows, machine-read registers, renovate.json, package.json files and the catalog. Dated records — ADRs, research reports, session notes, archives, the rename narratives in README files — are DELIBERATELY out of scope and are listed under `excludedPaths`. A frozen record is superseded, never rewritten.

_allowedSuffixesWhy: A dead repository NAME immediately followed by one of these is a different identifier that merely starts with the same characters. `Project_Cross_Platform_Apps_GITHUB_PAT` is the real key in the local vault and in tooling/ops/safe-rerun.mjs; renaming it would break `gh` auth for every ops script. This list is short on purpose — it is an exemption surface, and each entry must name a thing that genuinely still exists.

scan._globsWhy: Every one of these is READ BY A MACHINE. A dead name in any of them is acted on rather than merely read: a workflow dispatches against it, a register is joined on it, a package manifest resolves it. Prose is out of scope by construction — see excludedPaths.
scan._mjsAddedWhy: ⏱ 2026-09-08 — `tooling/**/*.mjs` was MISSING, and it is the strongest member of the set rather than the weakest. Every other glob names a file a machine READS; a .mjs under tooling/ is a file a machine EXECUTES, so a dead repository name on a live line there is not merely read aloud, it is acted on. Measured the day it was added: the six other globs reached 61 files; with this one the walk reads 291. The hole was real and had a name — `tooling/scripts/install-hooks.mjs:162` holds a dead repository name in an executable array and was invisible to this guard, which is exactly the shape the guard exists for. It is now VISIBLE and declared in `codeMentions` below, which is the difference between an exemption and a blind spot.
scan._commentStrippedWhy: A comment is not acted on, so it is not this guard's subject — the argument the YAML limb already makes at length, applied to the language the new glob admits. Without it this guard would have gone red on ~28 dated records of the very renames it enforces, INCLUDING ITS OWN HEADER, and a guard that forbids the record of its own defect is a guard people delete. The stripper is `stripSourceComments` from tooling/ci/text-reductions.mjs — the corpus's existing one, reused rather than rivalled — and it is offset- and line-preserving, so every reported line and column still points at the real byte. STRING LITERALS ARE STILL SCANNED, exactly as in YAML: a name is no less live for being quoted.

codeMentions.why: PRIVATE_WAS keeps the pre-2026-08-18 corpus location as EVIDENCE for the leftover branch's test, and lines 156-159 say nothing is ever installed into it. It is live code, not a comment, and it is the single hit that made adding the .mjs glob worth doing: before 2026-09-08 this guard could not see it at all.
a sentence inside a printed explanation naming where the private corpus moved to on 2026-08-18. It is prose that happens to live in a string rather than in a comment; nothing resolves it.
a printed WORKSPACE DOES NOT CONTAIN message recording that RENOVATE_REPOSITORIES named the now-deleted extensions repo until 2026-09-06. A dated record of the removal this guard enforces.
a printed sentence recording that the extensions repo was merged into this one on 2026-09-05 under ADR 067. Same class as the row above.

_codeMentionsWhy: THE RESIDUE AFTER COMMENTS ARE STRIPPED, DECLARED WITH A COUNT RATHER THAN WAIVED BY PATH. An entry excuses EXACTLY `count` occurrences in that file: MORE is a finding, because a new mention appeared that nobody argued for; FEWER is COVERAGE LOST, because the reason has expired and the row must retire with it. That asymmetry is the whole point — an excludedPaths entry blinds a whole file forever, and blinding tooling/scripts/install-hooks.mjs is precisely how the hole the .mjs glob just closed would have been re-opened under a politer name.
_excludedPathsWhy: DATED RECORDS and fixtures, each excluded for a stated reason, not for convenience. tooling/github-org.json carries removedSlot20260906_Chrome_Web_Store and deletionRecord20260819 under `records` — dated records OF the deaths this file lists, and the one place the old names must survive verbatim (moved there verbatim on 2026-09-25 from the retired store matrix, which held them until then). tooling/ops/register.json carries dated operational history. tooling/ci/test/ holds FIXTURES that deliberately name dead repos to prove guards catch them, this guard's own mutation test included. tooling/bricks/ is template source, not a live register. tooling/dead-repos.json is this file, which names every dead repo by definition and would otherwise be its own first finding.

_floorsMeasured.verify: node tooling/ci/assert-no-dead-repo-names.mjs   — the first line prints `<n> machine-read file(s) scanned against <m> dead repository name(s)`
_floorsMeasured.why: `files` was 8 against a measured 61 before `tooling/**/*.mjs` joined the scan set, and 8 against 291 after it — a floor two orders of magnitude under its subject cannot detect a scan that stopped scanning, which is the only thing a floor is for. Re-based to 240, which is ~18% under today's 291: enough headroom for the tooling tree to shrink through ordinary churn, not enough for a glob to silently stop matching. Raised in a commit of its own, AFTER the change that moved the measurement and while the tree it describes is green, because a floor that moves in the same commit as its subject cannot be read as evidence of either. `repos` is deliberately untouched at 11 against 11: `_theRule` says a name is never removed, so that floor has zero margin BY DESIGN and any drop is exit 2.

_floorsWhy: A scan that silently matched nothing must not read as a pass. If the walk finds fewer than `files` files, or the list holds fewer than `repos` names, the guard exits 2 CANNOT RUN rather than 0. Raise these when the tree grows; never lower them to make a run go green.
